transcript.text: Everyone, as you know, Cell 6 faulted during its scheduled setup and is currently unavailable. We have a customer order for 300 brackets from the current production campaign that needs to move forward. Cell 3 is idle and capable of welding the same bracket family using its manual fixture. I have the authority to approve a temporary route change and release this campaign on Cell 3, but per company procedure, I need to conduct a pre-release review with quality, maintenance, materials, and safety before I can sign off on the alternate-cell campaign. So let's go through that review now — can I get input from each of those functions on any concerns with routing this campaign to Cell 3?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a quality concern before we proceed. Yesterday I checked the customer drawing revision in the customer portal and found that release requires destructive testing of exactly 8 brackets and 100% dimensional inspection of the first exactly 20 brackets. I have not yet updated the campaign traveler with these requirements, so we need to make sure the traveler reflects these inspection and testing requirements before any production starts on Cell 3.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a maintenance concern before we route this to Cell 3. I inspected Cell 3 this morning and found wear in fixture F-19's jaws. The J-19 replacement kit is already in the crib, and replacing and validating the jaws will take exactly 3 maintenance hours. I have not yet opened the work order — I'll need to get that started before we can run production on Cell 3.

transcript.text: I can speak to materials. This morning I reconciled the physical blanks and confirmed that lot BQ-18 contains exactly 312 usable blanks — 300 for the customer order and exactly 12 to reserve for the required destructive and dimensional checks. The inventory adjustment is still pending in the materials system, so the system won't reflect the correct count yet, but physically we have exactly enough blanks to cover both the order and the inspection and testing requirements Victor just outlined.

transcript.text: I need to flag a safety concern before we route this campaign to Cell 3. I measured Cell 3's welding-fume extraction velocity at 0.72 m/s, which is below the 0.80 m/s minimum required for safe welding operations. The filter change will take exactly 2 hours, and after that I need to perform an airflow verification before any welding can begin. I have not yet issued the safety clearance for Cell 3, so we cannot start production until the filter is replaced, airflow is re-verified, and I issue that clearance.
